changes_made.explanation: Removed incorrectly extracted tasks (Retrieval-augmented Generation, Clinical Report Generation are not tasks but benchmark types; Dialogue generation not mentioned). Added actual tasks from benchmarks (summarization, report generation). Normalized model names with hyphens. Simplified outputs to reflect actual content.
Removed 'Hallucination rate (LLM-based)' as it's not an automatic metric but an LLM-as-judge evaluation. Kept ROUGE variants as they are distinct metrics used for different benchmarks.

Removed redundant/general terms ('LLM-based judgment' is the category, not a specific method; 'direct assessment' not mentioned). Removed 'conflicting spans' as it's part of the hallucination definition, not a separate criterion.
No human evaluation conducted, only LLM-based evaluation as confirmed by the paper.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on mitigating hallucinations through knowledge verification, not on developing new NLG tasks. The evaluation uses both automatic metrics (ROUGE) and LLM-as-judge (GPT-4) for hallucination detection and helpfulness scoring. The extracted metadata had several inaccuracies, including incorrectly categorized tasks and metrics that don't belong to the right categories.
